title: Matthew Chapter 14 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 14 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 14 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 14.

questions.question: In Matthew 14, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus
The daughter of Herodias danced before Herod
Herod promised to give the daughter whatever she asked
questions.correctAnswer: Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:1 states first, 'At that time Herod the tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus,' which is the earliest event mentioned.

questions.question: Who did Herod the tetrarch think Jesus was?
options: John the Baptist risen from the dead
A new king of the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: John the Baptist risen from the dead
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:2 states Herod said, 'This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead.'

questions.question: Why had Herod laid hold on John the Baptist and put him in prison?
options: For Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife
Due to his preaching in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: For Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:3 says, 'For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife.'

questions.question: What did John the Baptist say to Herod about Herodias?
options: It is not lawful for thee to have her
questions.correctAnswer: It is not lawful for thee to have her
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:4 states, 'For John said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.'

questions.question: Why did Herod not initially put John to death?
options: He feared the multitude because they counted John as a prophet
He was waiting for a better time
He was ordered by Pilate not to
He was secretly sympathetic to John
questions.correctAnswer: He feared the multitude because they counted John as a prophet
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:5 says, 'when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.'

questions.question: What occasion was being kept when the daughter of Herodias danced?
questions.correctAnswer: Herod's birthday
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:6 states, 'when Herod's birthday was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before them.'

questions.question: What did Herod promise to the daughter of Herodias after she danced?
options: To give her whatsoever she would ask
To give her a large sum of money
questions.correctAnswer: To give her whatsoever she would ask
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:7 says, 'he promised with an oath to give her whatsoever she would ask.'

questions.question: What did the daughter of Herodias ask for, being instructed by her mother?
options: John Baptist's head in a charger
questions.correctAnswer: John Baptist's head in a charger
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:8 states, 'she... said, Give me here John Baptist's head in a charger.'

questions.question: How did Herod feel when the daughter of Herodias asked for John the Baptist's head?
options: He was sorry, but gave it for the oath's sake
questions.correctAnswer: He was sorry, but gave it for the oath's sake
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:9 says, 'the king was sorry: nevertheless for the oath's sake... he commanded it to be given her.'

questions.question: Where was John the Baptist beheaded?
questions.correctAnswer: In the prison
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:10 states, 'he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.'

questions.question: Who took up John the Baptist's body and buried it?
questions.correctAnswer: His disciples
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:12 says, 'his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it.'

questions.question: John the Baptist's head was brought to whom?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:11 states, 'his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.'

questions.question: Herod feared the multitude because they counted John as a prophet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:5 says Herod feared the multitude because they counted John as a prophet.

questions.question: Herod gave the daughter of Herodias whatever she asked without hesitation.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:9 states that the king was sorry but gave the head for the oath's sake, showing hesitation.

questions.question: Jesus was present at Herod's birthday celebration where the daughter danced.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The text does not mention Jesus being present at Herod's birthday celebration (Matthew 14:6).

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 14 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 14 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus do when he saw the great multitude?
options: He was moved with compassion and healed their sick
questions.correctAnswer: He was moved with compassion and healed their sick
questions.explanation: This is correct as it states in Matthew 14:14 that Jesus was moved with compassion toward them and healed their sick.

questions.question: What does Matthew 14:16 promise will happen if Jesus' disciples obey and give the multitude something to eat?
options: They will be praised by the crowd
questions.correctAnswer: They need not depart
questions.explanation: Jesus said to his disciples in Matthew 14:16, 'They need not depart; give ye them to eat,' indicating that by following His command, the multitude will not need to leave.

questions.question: How many loaves and fishes did the disciples have to feed the multitude?
questions.correctAnswer: Five loaves and two fishes
questions.explanation: The disciples reported to Jesus in Matthew 14:17 that they had five loaves and two fishes.

questions.question: What did Jesus do with the loaves and fishes before distributing them?
options: He commanded the multitude to sit down
He gave them to the disciples directly
questions.correctAnswer: He blessed and broke them
questions.explanation: In Matthew 14:19, Jesus blessed, broke, and then gave the loaves to His disciples for distribution.

questions.question: According to Matthew 14:20, how much food was left after everyone ate?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve baskets full
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:20 states that after all had eaten, twelve baskets full of fragments were collected.

questions.question: What was the approximate number of men who ate from the loaves and fishes?
questions.correctAnswer: About 5,000 men
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:21 specifies that about five thousand men, not counting women and children, ate.

questions.question: What did Jesus do after sending the multitude away?
options: He went up into a mountain to pray
questions.correctAnswer: He went up into a mountain to pray
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:23 tells us that after sending the multitudes away, Jesus went up into a mountain apart to pray.

questions.question: What condition was the ship in when the disciples were in the midst of the sea?
questions.correctAnswer: It was tossed with waves
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:24 describes the ship as being tossed with waves because the wind was contrary.

questions.question: In what context did Jesus ask His disciples to give the multitude something to eat?
questions.correctAnswer: When it was evening
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:15 indicates that it was evening when the disciples told Jesus to send the multitude away, prompting His command to feed them.

questions.question: What does the feeding of the 5,000 teach about Jesus' compassion?
options: He only cares for the wealthy
He is indifferent to people's needs
He is compassionate and meets needs
He only performs miracles for His disciples
questions.correctAnswer: He is compassionate and meets needs
questions.explanation: The account in Matthew 14:14 shows Jesus' compassion for the multitude, leading Him to heal their sick and provide for their needs.

questions.question: Why did Herod fear putting John the Baptist to death?
options: He was afraid of the soldiers
He feared the multitude, who counted John as a prophet
He was warned by a dream
He wanted to avoid a scandal
questions.correctAnswer: He feared the multitude, who counted John as a prophet
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:5 explains that Herod feared the multitude because they held John the Baptist in high regard as a prophet.

questions.question: Jesus told His disciples to give the multitude something to eat. What does this suggest about faith?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires action
questions.explanation: By instructing His disciples to give the multitude food, Jesus was teaching them that faith is often demonstrated through action, as indicated by Matthew 14:16.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was alone when he healed the sick in the multitude.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false. Jesus was not alone; He was surrounded by the multitude as stated in Matthew 14:14.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were excited to send the multitude away after they had eaten.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false. The disciples suggested sending the multitude away because it was evening and they were concerned for their needs, as mentioned in Matthew 14:15.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples had no food to offer the multitude.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: This statement is false. The disciples had five loaves and two fishes to offer, as stated in Matthew 14:17.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 14 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 14.

questions.question: What did the disciples initially think when they saw Jesus walking on the sea in Matthew 14:26?
questions.correctAnswer: It is a spirit
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:26 states the disciples said, 'It is a spirit; and they cried out for fear.'

questions.question: How did Jesus respond to the disciples when they were afraid on the sea?
options: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid
Stay calm; I am with you
Do not worry; I will save you
questions.correctAnswer: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:27 quotes Jesus saying, 'Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.'

questions.question: What did Peter request from Jesus on the water according to Matthew 14:28?
options: Bid me come unto thee on the water
Teach me to walk on water
questions.correctAnswer: Bid me come unto thee on the water
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:28 records Peter saying, 'Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water.'

questions.question: What caused Peter to begin sinking while walking on the water?
questions.correctAnswer: Seeing the wind boisterous
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:30 states, 'But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink...'

questions.question: What did Jesus say to Peter when he began to sink on the water?
options: O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
questions.correctAnswer: O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:31 records Jesus saying, 'O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?'

questions.question: What was the reaction of those in the ship after Jesus and Peter entered it?
options: They worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God
They praised the wind for ceasing
questions.correctAnswer: They worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:33 says, 'Then they that were in the ship came and worshipped him, saying, Of a truth thou art the Son of God.'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'boisterous' (as used in Matthew 14:30) mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Violent or tempestuous
questions.explanation: In Matthew 14:30, 'boisterous' translates from a Greek word meaning 'violent or tempestuous,' describing the stormy wind Peter saw.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Matthew 14:25-33 where Jesus walks on water and Peter attempts to do the same?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: The passage in Matthew 14:25-33 demonstrates chiasmus, with a mirrored structure focusing on Jesus' approach, Peter's faith and doubt, and the disciples' worship.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed by Jesus walking on water in Matthew 14:25?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 77:19
questions.explanation: Psalm 77:19 speaks of God walking upon the waters, which echoes Jesus walking on the sea in Matthew 14:25.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage connects to the theme of Jesus as Son of God recognized by the disciples in Matthew 14:33?
questions.correctAnswer: John 20:28
questions.explanation: John 20:28 records Thomas calling Jesus 'My Lord and my God,' connecting to the recognition of Jesus' divine sonship in Matthew 14:33.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus walking on the sea in Matthew 14:25?
options: The disciples in a ship tossed by waves
Jesus praying alone on the mountain
Herod's beheading of John the Baptist
questions.correctAnswer: The disciples in a ship tossed by waves
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:24 describes 'the ship was now in the midst of the sea, tossed with waves,' immediately preceding Jesus walking on the sea in verse 25.

questions.question: What is the typological significance of Jesus allowing Peter to walk on water in Matthew 14:29?
options: It symbolizes faith overcoming natural laws
It represents the crossing of the Red Sea
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes faith overcoming natural laws
questions.explanation: Peter walking on water in Matthew 14:29 typologically symbolizes how faith can transcend natural limitations, affirming Jesus' divine authority.

questions.question: How does the healing ministry in Matthew 14:35-36 reflect Old Testament expectations of the Messiah?
options: It fulfills Isaiah 53:5's prophecy of healing by the Messiah's wounds
It replicates Moses' miracles in Egypt
It shows fulfillment of the Sinai covenant
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills Isaiah 53:5's prophecy of healing by the Messiah's wounds
questions.explanation: The healing of the diseased in Matthew 14:35-36 fulfills Isaiah 53:5's prophecy about the Messiah bearing our sicknesses and healing by his wounds.

questions.question: True or False: According to Matthew 14:36, only those who touched Jesus' garment were made perfectly whole.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:36 states, 'as many as touched were made perfectly whole,' confirming that touching Jesus' garment brought healing.

questions.question: True or False: In Matthew 14:2, Herod believed Jesus was John the Baptist returned from the dead because of the miracles Jesus was performing.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:2 shows Herod saying, 'This is John the Baptist; he is risen from the dead,' indicating Herod's belief but not an affirmation of it being true.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 14 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 14 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Matthew 14:2 teach about the nature of Jesus' miraculous works?
options: Jesus' miracles are evidence of his resurrection.
Jesus' miracles confirm his identity as John the Baptist reincarnated.
Jesus' miracles are signs of divine authority and power manifest in him.
Jesus' miracles stem from human wisdom and skill.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' miracles are signs of divine authority and power manifest in him.
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:2 shows that Herod mistakenly attributes Jesus' miracles to John the Baptist returned from the dead, implying that the works demonstrate divine power authenticating Jesus' mission rather than human origin.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sin and law does Matthew 14:4 teach through John's rebuke of Herod?
options: The doctrine of the inviolability of divine law in human relationships.
The doctrine that civil laws override moral laws.
The doctrine that personal desires justify breaking the law.
The doctrine that John endorsed Herod's marriage for political gain.
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of the inviolability of divine law in human relationships.
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:4 reveals that John confronts Herod for unlawfully marrying his brother's wife, emphasizing that God's moral law supersedes human political arrangements.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' compassion and healing ministry is taught in Matthew 14:14?
options: Jesus' compassion motivates his healing acts, reflecting divine mercy.
Jesus heals only those who have faith in him beforehand.
Healing is a secondary aspect of Jesus' ministry focused on teaching.
Jesus' healing serves primarily to attract crowds for political influence.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' compassion motivates his healing acts, reflecting divine mercy.
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:14 explicitly states that Jesus was moved with compassion toward the multitude and healed their sick, indicating mercy as a primary motive for his healing ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Matthew 14:27 specifically demonstrate when Jesus says, 'Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid'?
questions.correctAnswer: Immanence
questions.explanation: In Matthew 14:27, Jesus' reassurance reveals God's immanence—His presence with and care for His disciples even in fearful moments.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is particularly highlighted in Jesus' response to Peter's faltering faith in Matthew 14:31?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Jesus' immediate aid and gentle rebuke in Matthew 14:31 demonstrate divine longsuffering—patience with human weakness and doubt.

questions.question: How does the feeding of the five thousand in Matthew 14:19-20 connect with Old Testament themes?
options: It fulfills the theme of God providing manna to Israel in the wilderness.
It echoes the destruction of Jericho as a sign of conquest.
It represents the covenant with David about kingship.
It prefigures the exile of Israel to Babylon.
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the theme of God providing manna to Israel in the wilderness.
questions.explanation: The miraculous feeding in Matthew 14:19-20 recalls God's provision of manna in Exodus 16, reinforcing Jesus as the new provider and sustainer of God's people.

questions.question: How does Jesus walking on the sea in Matthew 14:25-27 prepare for the revelation of his divine identity in the Gospel?
options: It anticipates his authority over creation and nature.
It foreshadows his crucifixion and death.
It prefigures his role as a political revolutionary.
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates his authority over creation and nature.
questions.explanation: Jesus walking on the sea shows mastery over natural laws (Matthew 14:25-27), a divine prerogative, preparing for the fuller revelation of his identity as Son of God.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Matthew 14:13 and Matthew 14:23 teach about Jesus' pattern of ministry and prayer?
options: Jesus balances public ministry with solitary prayer, demonstrating dependence on the Father.
Jesus prefers isolation over ministering to the crowds.
Jesus prays only after miracles to seek approval.
Jesus relies solely on his own strength, avoiding prayer.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus balances public ministry with solitary prayer, demonstrating dependence on the Father.
questions.explanation: Both verses show Jesus withdrawing to pray after ministry events, indicating his dependence on communion with the Father as essential to his mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine is taught in Matthew 14:28 and Matthew 14:29 about faith and discipleship?
options: Faith requires active response and obedience to Jesus' call despite fear.
Faith is passive and requires no action.
Discipleship is based on social status, not faith.
Doubt is preferable to risking obedience.
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires active response and obedience to Jesus' call despite fear.
questions.explanation: Peter's request and Jesus' invitation (Matthew 14:28-29) illustrate that genuine faith involves stepping out in obedience even in uncertain or frightening circumstances.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about Jesus' identity and human weakness is conveyed in Matthew 14:30 and Matthew 14:31?
options: Jesus' divine aid is essential to sustain believers amid doubt and fear.
Human strength alone is sufficient to overcome trials.
Faith is irrelevant to Jesus' saving work.
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus' divine aid is essential to sustain believers amid doubt and fear.
questions.explanation: Peter's sinking due to fear and Jesus' saving hand (Matthew 14:30-31) teach that human frailty requires divine intervention for perseverance.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that the feeding miracle in Matthew 14:15-21 is merely a legend. What does this passage actually teach?
options: It teaches Jesus' real power to miraculously provide physical sustenance to large crowds.
It suggests that the story is a symbolic myth with no historical basis.
It implies Jesus used natural means to distribute food without miracles.
It denies Jesus' ability to meet physical needs.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches Jesus' real power to miraculously provide physical sustenance to large crowds.
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:15-21 describes a concrete miracle where Jesus multiplies loaves and fishes to feed thousands, affirming his divine provision and power.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine justice is taught in Matthew 14:10 regarding John the Baptist's execution?
options: God permits human injustice but ultimately judges sin.
God causes unjust deaths to punish prophets.
Justice is irrelevant in earthly affairs.
John's death was a divine reward.
questions.correctAnswer: God permits human injustice but ultimately judges sin.
questions.explanation: Matthew 14:10 records Herod's unjust execution of John, showing that evil men can act unjustly, but Scripture elsewhere teaches God's final judgment over all sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Jesus' healing of all who touched his garment in Matthew 14:36?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: The healing of many who touch Jesus' garment (Matthew 14:36) reveals God's mercy—compassionate intervention to restore the sick.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about faith and divine provision is taught in Matthew 14:16 and Matthew 14:17?
options: God provides abundantly even when human resources appear insufficient.
Faith requires large resources before God acts.
questions.correctAnswer: God provides abundantly even when human resources appear insufficient.
questions.explanation: Jesus' command to feed the multitude despite only five loaves and two fishes (Matthew 14:16-17) shows divine provision surpasses human limitation.

questions.question: How does Matthew 14:35-36 contribute to the narrative arc of Jesus' ministry and its reception in Galilean society?
options: It shows widespread faith in Jesus' healing power and growing public recognition.
It indicates rejection of Jesus by the people of Gennesaret.
It highlights Jesus' isolation from society.
It represents official opposition from religious leaders.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows widespread faith in Jesus' healing power and growing public recognition.
questions.explanation: The passage reports that people brought all the diseased to Jesus and believed touching his garment would heal them, indicating increasing faith and acceptance.
